app-server-registry.title: Experimental enum-variant gate for granular approval policy never fires (gating bypass)
app-server-registry.rustEvidence: app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/shared.rs:168 marks the `AskForApproval::Granular` enum variant `#[experimental("askForApproval.granular")]`. ThreadStart/ThreadResume/ThreadFork/TurnStart all use `inspect_params: true` (common.rs:445-461,730-735) so `ClientRequest::experimental_reason()` recurses into params; message_processor.rs:792-796 rejects with `invalid_request(experimental_required_message(reason))` => -32600 `"askForApproval.granular requires experimentalApi capability"` when the connection did not negotiate experimentalApi. Confirmed by tests.rs:1719-1736 (`client_request_thread_start_granular_approval_policy_is_marked_experimental` => reason `Some("askForApproval.granular")`).
app-server-registry.swiftStatus: Sources/Supervisor/RequestRouter.swift:9373-9376 `presentFields(_:)` returns ONLY `Array(obj.keys)` (top-level keys) and never emits a `"field=variant"` marker. ExperimentalGate.rejectionDescriptor (Sources/WireProtocol/ExperimentalGate.swift:154-168) only matches enum variants via `if f.contains("=") { if enumVariants.contains(f) ... }`, and `defaultEnumVariants` (line 143-146: `askForApproval=granular`, `approvalPolicy=granular`) is therefore dead code. A non-experimental connection sending `thread/start` (or resume/fork/turn/start) with `approvalPolicy: {"granular": {...}}` is NOT rejected; the granular value is then silently dropped by `approvalPolicy(from:)` (RequestRouter.swift:2453-2463, which only reads a string or `type`/`mode` key).
app-server-registry.description: Upstream rejects a non-experimental client that supplies a granular approval policy on thread/start, thread/resume, thread/fork, or turn/start with -32600 `askForApproval.granular requires experimentalApi capability`. The Swift port accepts the request instead, because the experimental enum-variant gate is never evaluated against the params value (presentFields only yields top-level keys). Additionally, even if it did fire, the descriptor Swift would build (`<method>.approvalPolicy=granular`) differs from upstream's fixed reason `askForApproval.granular`, so the error message would also diverge.
app-server-registry.fixRecommendation: In Sources/Supervisor/RequestRouter.swift, extend `presentFields` (or add a typed-params inspection) so that when `approvalPolicy`/`askForApproval` (and nested profile approval-policy fields) carry the `granular` variant, it appends the marker `askForApproval=granular`. Then change `ExperimentalGate.rejectionDescriptor` so that for enum-variant matches it returns the fixed upstream reason `askForApproval.granular` (not `<method>.<marker>`), matching `experimental_required_message`. Keep only `askForApproval=granular` in `defaultEnumVariants` (the `approvalPolicy=granular` alias should map to the same reason).

app-server-events.title: Transient stream errors (willRetry=true) incorrectly flip thread status to systemError
app-server-events.rustEvidence: app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs:883-942 — terminal EventMsg::Error calls thread_watch_manager.note_system_error(...) (line 884-886) and emits ErrorNotification{will_retry:false}; the SEPARATE EventMsg::StreamError handler (line 926-942) emits ErrorNotification{will_retry:true} and explicitly does NOT touch thread status ('We don't need to update the turn summary store for stream errors as they are intermediate error states for retries, but we notify the client'). thread_status.rs:172-180 note_system_error sets running=false, has_system_error=true.
app-server-events.swiftStatus: Sources/Supervisor/SessionSupervisor.swift:400-414 applyStatusEffect treats ALL .error notifications identically: `case .error: updateStatusFacts(tid) { $0.running = false; $0.hasSystemError = true }` with no willRetry check. SessionEngine.swift:1872,1900,2434,2934 emit .error(..., willRetry: true, ...) for transient StreamError retries, which then route through this blanket status effect.
app-server-events.description: Upstream only mutates thread status (running=false, has_system_error=true → ThreadStatus::SystemError) on TERMINAL EventMsg::Error, never on retryable EventMsg::StreamError. The Swift supervisor flips the thread to systemError and clears running on EVERY .error notification, including transient willRetry=true stream errors. A frontend watching thread/status/changed will see the thread bounce to systemError mid-turn during a normal retry, diverging from upstream where the status stays Active across retries.
app-server-events.fixRecommendation: In SessionSupervisor.swift applyStatusEffect, gate the status mutation on willRetry: `case .error(_, _, let willRetry, _): if !willRetry { updateStatusFacts(tid) { $0.running = false; $0.hasSystemError = true } }`. Retryable stream errors must leave running/hasSystemError unchanged (parity with upstream StreamError handler).

model-client.title: Stream that ends without response.completed is treated as success instead of a terminal stream error
model-client.rustEvidence: codex-rs/codex-api/src/sse/responses.rs:422-428 — when the eventsource stream returns Ok(None) (closed) and no prior response_error was recorded, process_sse sends Err(ApiError::Stream("stream closed before response.completed")). Test error_when_missing_completed (responses.rs:701-727) asserts a 2nd event Err(ApiError::Stream("stream closed before response.completed")) is emitted. Only ResponseEvent::Completed (responses.rs:471-477) terminates the stream cleanly.
model-client.swiftStatus: Sources/ModelClient/URLSessionResponsesClient.swift:282-287 — after the byte loop ends, `guard sawAny else { ...no SSE... }` then `cont.finish()` with NO error when frames were seen but no response.completed/failed arrived. Same in Sources/ModelClient/OpenAIResponsesClient.swift:814-825. StreamMapper.swift:30-37 also finishes with .done (no error) when the upstream AsyncStream ends normally. SessionEngine.swift:2749-2821 only sets endTurn/followUp inside the .completed case, so a truncated stream leaves the turn ambiguous (neither flag set) and no retry is triggered.
model-client.description: Upstream guarantees that a stream which delivers partial output but never emits response.completed is converted into a retryable ApiError::Stream, which feeds the core retry/turn loop. The Swift port silently finishes the stream as a success on both the URLSession (production macOS) and curl transports, so a truncated/aborted-mid-turn response is accepted without retry and the turn loop neither ends nor follows up.
model-client.fixRecommendation: In both URLSessionResponsesClient.readSSE and OpenAIResponsesClient's reader thread, track a `sawCompleted` flag set inside the response.completed/failed handling; after the read loop ends, if `sawAny && !sawCompleted`, call cont.finish(throwing: ModelError("stream closed before response.completed", retryable: true)) instead of cont.finish(). (Keep the existing `!sawAny` -> non-retryable "no SSE" path.)

model-client.title: No per-event SSE idle timeout (silent stream hangs to full turn deadline)
model-client.rustEvidence: codex-rs/codex-api/src/sse/responses.rs:410-434 — each poll wraps `timeout(idle_timeout, stream.next())`; on elapse it sends Err(ApiError::Stream("idle timeout waiting for SSE")) and returns. idle_timeout is provider.stream_idle_timeout (endpoint/responses.rs:147-150 passes self.session.provider().stream_idle_timeout).
model-client.swiftStatus: Sources/ModelClient/URLSessionResponsesClient.swift:60-62,102-104 — only timeoutIntervalForRequest/Resource = turnDeadline (clamped up to 24h) is set; the `for try await byte in bytes` loop (line 257) has no inter-event deadline. grep across Sources shows no SSE idleTimeout in any Responses client.
model-client.description: Upstream aborts a stream that goes silent between events after stream_idle_timeout with a retryable error, allowing fast recovery. The Swift Responses clients have no inter-event idle timeout, so a server that opens the stream then stalls will block up to the entire turn deadline before any timeout fires.
model-client.fixRecommendation: Wrap each await on the byte stream with a per-event deadline (e.g. via a Task with Task.sleep race or a withTimeout helper) using a provider-configured idle timeout, finishing with ModelError("idle timeout waiting for SSE", retryable: true) on elapse.

model-client.title: Top-level `error` data frame is treated as a fatal non-retryable error instead of being ignored
model-client.rustEvidence: codex-rs/codex-api/src/sse/responses.rs:145-158 — ResponsesStreamEvent has NO `error` field; process_responses_event (266-394) only branches on `kind` strings (response.failed, etc.). A bare {"error":{...}} data frame with no recognized `type` falls into the `_ =>` arm (391-393): trace!("unhandled") and Ok(None) — i.e. ignored, stream continues.
model-client.swiftStatus: Sources/ModelClient/URLSessionResponsesClient.swift:304-308 and OpenAIResponsesClient.swift:558-563 — at the top of each frame, `if let err = obj["error"] ... cont.finish(throwing: ModelError(msg, retryable: false)); return true` aborts the stream non-retryably for any frame carrying a top-level `error` key.
model-client.description: Upstream only classifies errors carried inside a response.failed event's response.error; a stray top-level `error` data frame is ignored and the stream continues. The Swift transports terminate the whole stream as a non-retryable failure on any top-level `error` key, which diverges from upstream's tolerant behavior and could turn an ignorable provider frame into a hard turn failure.
model-client.fixRecommendation: Remove (or restrict) the top-level obj["error"] short-circuit in both readSSE/mapEvent and the curl reader; rely on the response.failed handler (which already calls classifyResponseFailed) so non-standard top-level error frames are ignored as upstream does.

sandbox-safety-policy.title: Accepted applyNetworkPolicyAmendment is decoded but never persisted as a network_rule
sandbox-safety-policy.rustEvidence: core/src/session/mod.rs:1855-1891 handle a NetworkPolicyAmendment by calling ExecPolicyManager::append_network_rule_and_update (core/src/exec_policy.rs:431-475), which calls blocking_append_network_rule (execpolicy/src/amend.rs:85-125) to write a `network_rule(host=..., protocol=..., decision=...)` line and updates the in-memory policy. The protocol/decision/justification are derived from the NetworkApprovalContext via execpolicy_network_rule_amendment (core/src/network_policy_decision.rs:74-102).
sandbox-safety-policy.swiftStatus: Sources/HarnessCore/SessionEngine.swift:1063, 1092, 1127 — every `case .accept, .applyNetworkPolicyAmendment:` collapses the network-amendment decision into a plain re-run/escalate (`r = await escalated()`) and discards the associated NetworkPolicyAmendment payload. There is NO call to RulesStore.appendNetworkRule / ApprovedRuleStore.insertNetworkRule anywhere in HarnessCore (grep: insertNetworkRule/appendNetworkRule appear only in ExecPolicy.swift/RulesStore.swift definitions, never invoked from the approval flow). The host/protocol/justification (execpolicy_network_rule_amendment) is never derived.
sandbox-safety-policy.description: Upstream: when the user accepts a network-policy amendment, codex persists a network_rule(...) line to default.rules and updates the live policy so future requests to that host are auto-allowed/denied. Swift: the amendment is dropped — the command is re-run once but the host approval is not remembered across requests or restarts, diverging from the documented one-click 'allow this host' behavior. The RulesStore.appendNetworkRule machinery exists but is never wired to the accept path.
sandbox-safety-policy.fixRecommendation: In SessionEngine.swift, split the `.applyNetworkPolicyAmendment(amendment)` case from `.accept`: derive protocol from the NetworkApprovalContext (http/https→https_connect/socks5_tcp/socks5_udp) and decision from amendment.action (allow→.safe, deny→.forbidden), build the justification ('Allow/Deny <protocol_label> access to <host>' per network_policy_decision.rs:95), then call RulesStore.appendNetworkRule(codexHome:host:proto:decision:justification:) and reload/merge the in-memory ExecPolicy network rules before re-running.

apply-patch.title: Apply is not all-or-nothing: multi-file patch partially mutates FS on a later-hunk failure
apply-patch.rustEvidence: core/src/tools/handlers/apply_patch.rs:329-358 parses, then calls codex_apply_patch::verify_apply_patch_args (invocation.rs:161-233) which for EVERY hunk reads the file and computes new contents (Update via unified_diff_from_chunks→derive_new_contents_from_chunks→compute_replacements; Delete via read_file_text) WITHOUT writing anything. Any hunk failure returns MaybeApplyPatchVerified::CorrectnessError (invocation.rs:191,214) so NO file is touched. Only after all hunks verify does apply_patch::apply_patch (core/src/apply_patch.rs:33) write. apply_hunks_to_files (lib.rs:393-547) then performs the writes.
apply-patch.swiftStatus: Sources/Tools/ApplyPatch.swift:140-230 apply() loops over files and writes/deletes each one inline as it iterates; a context-mismatch or missing-target in file N throws AFTER files 1..N-1 were already written/removed to disk. ToolRouter.swift:585-594 explicitly documents this: "The port's applier is not all-or-nothing, so a multi-file patch can commit earlier files before throwing on a later one".
apply-patch.description: Upstream verifies all hunks in-memory before any filesystem mutation, so a patch where a later file fails to match leaves the workspace untouched. Swift mutates earlier files before discovering the later failure, leaving a partially-applied workspace. A frontend that relies on apply_patch failure meaning "no changes were made" will see a corrupted/partial tree.
apply-patch.fixRecommendation: Split ApplyPatch into a verify phase and an apply phase: in apply(), first run a pass that reads each target and computes all new contents / validates all context matches (reusing deriveNewContents/computeReplacements and the delete/update existence checks) WITHOUT writing; only if every file verifies, perform the writes/removes in a second pass. Mirror verify_apply_patch_args + apply_hunks_to_files separation.

apply-patch.title: Missing-delete-target error uses wrong wording and omits OS error suffix
apply-patch.rustEvidence: On the handler path a missing delete target fails during verification at invocation.rs:188-198: ApplyPatchError::IoError(IoError{ context: format!("Failed to read {}", path.display()), source: e }). IoError Display is "{context}: {source}" (lib.rs:81), and path is the ABSOLUTE resolved path. Model sees "apply_patch verification failed: Failed to read /abs/path: <os error>".
apply-patch.swiftStatus: ApplyPatch.swift:170-176 throws ApplyPatchError.targetMissing("Failed to delete file \(full)") — wording "Failed to delete file" (not "Failed to read") and no trailing ": <os error>". ToolRouter.swift:601 wraps it as "apply_patch verification failed: Failed to delete file /abs/path".
apply-patch.description: The Swift port reproduces the non-verify CLI path's "Failed to delete file" text (lib.rs:427), but the production handler reaches the verify path first, which reports "Failed to read {abs}: {source}". Both the verb and the missing ": {os error}" suffix diverge from what a real client receives.
apply-patch.fixRecommendation: For Delete with a missing target, change ApplyPatch.swift:175 to surface "Failed to read \(full): \(underlyingErrno)" to match invocation.rs:193 + IoError Display. If the literal OS error text cannot be reproduced, at minimum change the prefix to "Failed to read".

apply-patch.title: Missing-update-target error omits the trailing OS error text
apply-patch.rustEvidence: derive_new_contents_from_chunks (lib.rs:663-668) maps a read failure to ApplyPatchError::IoError(IoError{ context: format!("Failed to read file to update {}", path_abs.display()), source: err }). Display = "{context}: {source}" (lib.rs:81). Model sees "apply_patch verification failed: Failed to read file to update /abs/path: <os error>".
apply-patch.swiftStatus: ApplyPatch.swift:188-194 throws targetMissing("Failed to read file to update \(full)") — context matches and uses the absolute path, but omits the ": <os error>" suffix that upstream's IoError Display appends.
apply-patch.description: The leading context string and absolute-path usage are correct, but the trailing ": {source}" io-error message that upstream always appends is dropped, so the model-facing text is not byte-identical.
apply-patch.fixRecommendation: Append the underlying error description, e.g. throw targetMissing("Failed to read file to update \(full): \(osErrorString)"). Same treatment for the delete case (previous finding).

apply-patch.title: Fuzzy context-mismatch and expected-lines errors render relative path instead of absolute
apply-patch.rustEvidence: compute_replacements is called with path_abs.as_path() (lib.rs:678), so both error strings use the ABSOLUTE path: "Failed to find context '{ctx}' in {path}" (lib.rs:714-718) and "Failed to find expected lines in {path}:\n{old_lines}" (lib.rs:771-775).
apply-patch.swiftStatus: ApplyPatch.swift:195-196 calls deriveNewContents(..., path: f.path) with the RELATIVE patch path; computeReplacements then emits "Failed to find context '\(ctx)' in \(path)" (line 723-724) and "Failed to find expected lines in \(path):\n..." (line 759-761) with that relative path.
apply-patch.description: The two most common apply-time fuzzy-match failures surface the relative path (e.g. 'src/foo.rs') where upstream surfaces the absolute resolved path. This is inconsistent even within the Swift port, since its delete/update missing-target errors already use the absolute path.
apply-patch.fixRecommendation: Pass the absolute `full` path (not f.path) into deriveNewContents/computeReplacements for the error-message rendering so the context-mismatch and expected-lines strings match upstream's path.display() output.

apply-patch.title: seek_sequence trim passes use a different whitespace set than Rust
apply-patch.rustEvidence: seek_sequence.rs:44 uses str::trim_end() and :57 str::trim(), which trim by Unicode White_Space (does NOT include U+00A0/NBSP, U+2007, etc.; those are only collapsed in the final normalise() pass at :76-94). The rstrip/trim passes therefore do not treat NBSP-like spaces as trimmable.
apply-patch.swiftStatus: ApplyPatch.swift:607-617 trimEnd uses CharacterSet.whitespaces and fullTrim uses .whitespacesAndNewlines. CharacterSet.whitespaces is category Zs + tab and DOES include U+00A0 and other Zs spaces, so the Swift rstrip/trim passes trim characters that Rust's trim() leaves intact.
apply-patch.description: For lines containing non-breaking or other Unicode spaces at their edges, the Swift trim/rstrip passes can match where Rust would only match (if at all) in the later normalise pass — a behavioral edge difference in fuzzy matching. Extremely low traffic (requires exotic spaces at line boundaries), so cosmetic in practice.
apply-patch.fixRecommendation: Restrict trimEnd/fullTrim to the ASCII whitespace set Rust's trim actually removes (space, \t, \n, \r, \x0B, \x0C) instead of CharacterSet.whitespaces(AndNewlines), leaving Zs/NBSP normalisation to the existing normalise() pass.

config.title: Project-local config discovery walks to filesystem root when no root marker matches (over-includes ancestor .codex configs)
config.rustEvidence: config/src/loader/mod.rs:1070-1092 find_project_root: `if project_root_markers.is_empty() { return Ok(cwd.clone()); }` and after the ancestor scan with no match `Ok(cwd.clone())`. load_project_layers (mod.rs:1134-1147) then walks only cwd..=project_root inclusive, so with empty/no-match markers exactly one dir (cwd) is checked for .codex/config.toml.
config.swiftStatus: Config.swift:760-786 loadProjectLocalLayers: the walk loop only `break`s when `!effectiveMarkers.isEmpty` AND a marker file exists; with an empty marker list or when no marker is ever found it falls through to `if parent == cur { break }`, i.e. it walks every ancestor up to '/'. The comment at :760-761 claims the walk is disabled for empty markers, but the code does the opposite.
config.description: Upstream bounds the project layer search to `cwd` itself whenever the marker set is empty or no marker is found in any ancestor. Swift instead reads `.codex/config.toml` from EVERY ancestor up to the filesystem root in those cases. This both changes which project configs apply and is a scope/security concern: an unrelated parent directory's `.codex/config.toml` (a repository-derived, denylist-limited layer) gets merged in when it should not.
config.fixRecommendation: In Config.swift loadProjectLocalLayers, replicate find_project_root: if effectiveMarkers.isEmpty, the project root is `cwd` (collect only [cwd]); otherwise scan ancestors for a marker and if none matches, set the project root to `cwd` (collect only [cwd]). Only when a marker matches should the walk include ancestors from cwd up to (and including) that matched dir.

config.rustEvidence: config_toml.rs:648-679 ToolsToml.web_search uses deserialize_optional_web_search_tool_config: a bool value (WebSearchToolConfigInput::Enabled) is intentionally mapped to None; only a config table survives. Test config_rpc.rs:297-323 config_read_ignores_bool_web_search_tool_config asserts `config.tools.web_search == None`.

config.title: config/read.config omits non-v2 ConfigToml Option fields that upstream serializes as explicit null
config.rustEvidence: config_manager_service.rs:129-137 serializes the effective `ConfigToml` then deserializes into ApiConfig; ConfigToml (config_toml.rs:144-500) has no container-level skip_serializing_if, so every Option field with no `skip` (e.g. `notify`, `default_permissions`, `permissions`, `auto_review`, `include_permissions_instructions`, `cli_auth_credentials_store`, ...) serializes as `null` and flows into ApiConfig.additional (v2/config.rs:283-284).
config.swiftStatus: Config.swift:331-345 configProjectionJSON only force-emits the v2 named fields (v2ConfigNamedFields, :307-315) as null; all other ConfigToml Option fields are emitted only if present in the merged map, so an unset `notify`/`auto_review`/`default_permissions`/etc. is absent rather than `null`.
config.description: For a minimal config, upstream's `config/read.config` contains dozens of explicit-null keys for the non-v2 ConfigToml Option fields; the Swift projection omits those keys entirely. A frontend that distinguishes key-present-as-null from key-absent will observe a different object shape. (Typed deserialization tolerates both, which limits impact.)
config.fixRecommendation: In configProjectionJSON, after the v2 named-field pass, also emit `.null` for every ConfigToml top-level Option field that lacks a serde default and is not already present (i.e. the configTomlTopLevelKeys minus the always-serialized maps/defaults), matching upstream's full-struct serialization.

config.title: config/read response sets layers:null instead of omitting the field when includeLayers is false
config.rustEvidence: app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/config.rs:374-375 ConfigReadResponse.layers: `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] pub layers: Option<Vec<ConfigLayer>>` — the `layers` key is absent from the JSON when include_layers is false.
config.swiftStatus: RequestRouter.swift:1952-1958 sets `layersJSON = .null` in the else branch and always includes `"layers": layersJSON` in the reply object, so the wire response carries `"layers": null`.
config.description: Upstream omits the `layers` key entirely when not requested; Swift always emits it (as null). A client schema expecting `layers` to be absent (optional) vs explicitly null may diverge.
config.fixRecommendation: Only insert the `layers` key into the config/read reply object when params.includeLayers == true; otherwise leave it out (do not emit an explicit null).

config.title: No configWarning notification emitted for project-local ignored (denylisted) config keys
config.rustEvidence: loader/mod.rs:1203-1218 sanitize_project_config returns ignored keys → project_ignored_config_keys_warning (mod.rs:892-907) → surfaced as startup_warnings; app-server/src/lib.rs:582-593 turns each into a ConfigWarningNotification with method `configWarning` (app-server-protocol/.../common.rs:1512).
config.swiftStatus: ABSENT — Config.swift:677-679 applyDenylist silently removes denied keys with no warning collection; grep for `configWarning`/`ConfigWarningNotification` in Sources/ returns nothing.

mcp.title: tools/call requests omit the upstream-mandatory `_meta.threadId` (and sandbox-state) request metadata
mcp.rustEvidence: core/src/mcp_tool_call.rs:561-562 `let request_meta = with_mcp_tool_call_thread_id_meta(request_meta, &sess.conversation_id.to_string());` then :576-582 passes it to `sess.call_tool(...)`. The key is `const MCP_TOOL_THREAD_ID_META_KEY: &str = "threadId";` (core/src/mcp_tool_call.rs:986) and the helper (1075-1097) unconditionally inserts `threadId` into the request `_meta` (creating the object when meta is None). rmcp threads this through CallToolRequestParams as request-level `_meta` (rmcp-client/src/rmcp_client.rs:562-595). It is also augmented with sandbox-state meta (mcp_tool_call.rs:563-570).
mcp.swiftStatus: Sources/MCP/McpManager.swift:63-74 `McpToolProxy.run` calls `client.callTool(tool, argumentsJSON: call.argumentsJSON, elicitationHandler: elicitationHandler)` with NO `meta`, so the `meta`-carrying overload (McpClient.swift:970-983 / McpHttpClient.swift:887-914) never receives a threadId. grep for threadId/_meta injection in Sources/ finds none in the MCP call path. Every Swift `tools/call` therefore goes out with no `_meta` (or only a model-supplied one), never the `threadId`.
mcp.description: Upstream injects `_meta.threadId = <conversation_id>` into the params of EVERY `tools/call` request (and may add sandbox-state meta). The Swift port sends `tools/call` with no `_meta.threadId`. A server (e.g. codex_apps connectors, or any server that correlates calls to a conversation) that keys on `_meta.threadId` will not receive it, changing the observable request wire shape on every tool call.
mcp.fixRecommendation: In Sources/MCP/McpManager.swift `McpToolProxy.run` (and/or its initializer), thread a conversation/thread id into the proxy and build `meta: ["threadId": threadId]`, passing it to `client.callTool(tool, argumentsJSON:, meta:, elicitationHandler:)`. The McpClient/McpHttpClient already place `params["_meta"] = meta` when non-empty, so wiring the threadId through the proxy is sufficient. The thread id is already available at the session layer (codex-session/main.swift uses `c.threadId`).

mcp.title: Client always advertises elicitation sub-capabilities {"form":{},"url":{}} instead of the default empty {}
mcp.rustEvidence: The elicitation capability is feature-gated: core/src/config/mod.rs:1282-1290 and core/src/session/session.rs:1027-1031 set `client_elicitation_capability = if features.enabled(Feature::AuthElicitation) { ElicitationCapability { form: Some(default), url: Some(default) } } else { ElicitationCapability::default() }`. `Feature::AuthElicitation.default_enabled() == false` and stage `UnderDevelopment` (features/src/tests.rs:297-298). The struct uses `skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"` on both `form` and `url` (rmcp-0.15.0/src/model.rs:209-216), so the DEFAULT wire value is `"elicitation": {}`. initialize always sets `elicitation: Some(client_elicitation_capability)` (codex-mcp/src/rmcp_client.rs:480).
mcp.swiftStatus: Sources/MCP/McpClient.swift:33-36 `elicitationCapability` is a static constant `["form": [:], "url": [:]]`, sent unconditionally by both transports (McpClient.swift:906-909 initialize; McpHttpClient.swift:855-859 initialize). There is no AuthElicitation feature gate.
mcp.description: By default (AuthElicitation off) upstream advertises `"elicitation": {}`; the Swift client always advertises `"elicitation": {"form":{},"url":{}}` (the AuthElicitation-enabled form). This over-advertises URL/form sub-capabilities in the initialize handshake, which can prompt a server to issue URL/OAuth elicitations it would not otherwise send under the default Codex configuration.
mcp.fixRecommendation: Default `McpClientInfo.elicitationCapability` to an empty object `[:]` (matching `ElicitationCapability::default()`), and only emit `{"form":{},"url":{}}` when an AuthElicitation-equivalent flag is enabled. Keep the `elicitation` key always present (upstream always sets `Some(...)`).

mcp.title: Local stdio server silently drops `env_vars` entries with source="remote" instead of failing the launch
mcp.rustEvidence: rmcp-client/src/utils.rs:50-58 `local_stdio_env_var_names` returns Err for a local stdio server when any env_vars entry uses remote source: `return Err(anyhow!("env_vars entry `{}` uses source `remote`, which requires remote MCP stdio", remote_var.name()))`. This propagates out of `create_env_for_mcp_server` (utils.rs:12-25) and fails the stdio launch.
mcp.swiftStatus: Sources/MCP/McpClient.swift:1073-1077 `buildStdioEnvironment` iterates `for item in envVars where !item.isRemoteSource` — i.e. it silently skips remote-source entries and proceeds to launch the server normally; there is no error path.
mcp.description: Upstream treats a remote-source env_var on a local stdio server as a hard configuration error and refuses to start the server; the Swift port silently ignores the entry and starts the server anyway. The observable difference is a server that upstream would mark Failed comes up Ready in the port with the named variable missing.
mcp.fixRecommendation: In Sources/MCP/McpClient.swift `start()`/`buildStdioEnvironment`, detect any `config.envVars` entry with `isRemoteSource == true` for a non-remote (local) launch and throw `McpError.spawn`/mark the server failed with the upstream message `env_vars entry '<name>' uses source 'remote', which requires remote MCP stdio`, rather than dropping it.

mcp.title: Tool-argument validation error text differs from upstream ("...got {value}" suffix dropped)
mcp.rustEvidence: rmcp-client/src/rmcp_client.rs:553-560: non-object arguments produce `anyhow!("MCP tool arguments must be a JSON object, got {other}")`, and :562-569 `_meta` non-object produces `"MCP tool request _meta must be a JSON object, got {other}"`.

auth.title: account/login/start apiKey + chatgptAuthTokens failures return invalid_request (-32600) instead of internal_error (-32603), and the chatgptAuthTokens message text differs

auth.title: account/read returns account:null on a recorded refresh failure where upstream would still return the cached account

persistence-rollout.title: Tool-call / file-change history items are persisted in a non-upstream native envelope (not a RolloutItem) and are dropped when read by upstream codex
persistence-rollout.rustEvidence: rollout/src/policy.rs:67-85 should_persist_response_item returns true for FunctionCall/LocalShellCall/CustomToolCall/CustomToolCallOutput/WebSearchCall/etc.; recorder.rs:842-863 load_rollout_items only accepts lines that parse as RolloutLine (serde tag type+payload). A line lacking a `type` field is counted as a parse error and dropped (recorder.rs:865-868).
persistence-rollout.swiftStatus: Sources/Persistence/Rollout.swift:764-784 rustRolloutLine emits the upstream `response_item` envelope ONLY for .agentMessage/.reasoning; all other .item variants `return nil` and fall through to the native Swift `RolloutRecord.encode` (lines 175-251) which writes `{"t":"item","turnId":...,"item":{...}}` (no `type`/`payload`). Swift's own reader handles this, but upstream load_rollout_items would drop these lines.
persistence-rollout.description: Upstream persists ALL tool/exec/web-search ResponseItems as `response_item` rollout lines so any reader can replay full model history. The Swift port only emits the upstream wire shape for assistant-message and reasoning items; command-execution, file-change, collab-tool-call items are written in a Swift-private `{"t":"item"}` envelope that upstream's `from_value::<RolloutLine>` cannot parse. A Swift-written thread containing tool calls is faithfully replayable by the Swift server itself but loses those items if read by upstream codex.
persistence-rollout.fixRecommendation: In Rollout.swift rustRolloutLine, extend threadItemToResponseItem to map .commandExecution→function_call/local_shell_call, .fileChange→custom_tool_call/apply_patch, .collabAgentToolCall→function_call, and emit them as `response_item` lines (matching should_persist_response_item) instead of returning nil. If full cross-tool fidelity is out of scope, document explicitly that Swift rollouts are not upstream-readable when they contain tool history.

hooks.title: HookRunSummary.statusMessage carries outcome-derived text instead of the configured handler status_message
hooks.rustEvidence: hooks/src/engine/dispatcher.rs:79 (running_summary) and :132 (completed_summary) both set `status_message: handler.status_message.clone()` — i.e. the configured `statusMessage` field from hooks.json, emitted unchanged regardless of run outcome. ConfiguredHandler.status_message originates from discovery.rs:436/463/485 (the hook's declared statusMessage).

The completed summary (line 1071) sets statusMessage from that. The running summary (line 1054-1057) passes no statusMessage at all (defaults nil). Swift instead leaves it nil on started and fills it with the run's stop-reason/block-reason/error on completed. hooks.title: Stop-block continuation reason emitted as `stop`-kind entry instead of upstream `feedback`-kind
hooks.rustEvidence: hooks/src/events/stop.rs:171-184 (decision:block path) and :201-211 (exit-code-2 path) push `HookOutputEntry { kind: HookOutputEntryKind::Feedback, text: reason }` for the Stop continuation reason; the `Stop`-kind entry (:160-166) is reserved ONLY for the continue:false stop_reason.
